LM Studio has added Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model to its AI agent platform Bionic, offering multimodal input, a 1 million token context window, and pricing significantly lower than GLM-5.2. Details below.

LM Studio quickly adds GLM-5.3-Flash to Bionic platform

Since its initial launch in mid-July, LM Studio has continued to expand the models and features available on its Bionic platform. The platform is available for Mac and Windows and is used for agent tasks such as coding, research, and handling documents and files.

LM Studio Bionic can run models locally or use cloud-based models hosted on servers in the United States, with the latter protected by a strict zero data retention policy.

Shortly after launching LM Studio Bionic, the company added support for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3. Today, the company officially launched cloud support for Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model, which LM Studio says runs at up to 10 times lower cost than GLM-5.2.

LM Studio's announcement came just hours after the official release of GLM-5.3-Flash. The model had previously attracted considerable attention when it was tested anonymously under the code name "Ox Alpha" on OpenCode and OpenRouter.

GLM-5.3-Flash is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 320 billion parameters, activating 18 billion parameters per pass, supporting image and text input, with a 1 million token context window.

On multiple benchmark tests highlighted by Z.ai, GLM-5.3-Flash outperforms GLM-5.2, with overall performance broadly comparable to frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek.

For more information on how to use GLM-5.3-Flash on LM Studio Bionic, please follow this link.
